x: Wetlands Protection Act file #5-1127; recorded Bk 33797 Pg 168 (Jan 13, 2015). Sets the perpetual conservation conditions on the site.

t: Planning Board OSRD Site Plan Decision
x: Beverly Planning Board approves the Open Space Residential Design subdivision (Bk 33792 Pg 502), with the definitive-subdivision approval (Pg 499) and Special Permit #137-14 allowing a fee in lieu of on-site affordable units (Pg 507) — all recorded 1/12/2015. Plan by Hayes Engineering — Plan No. 73, Plan Book 446.

Declaration of Trust (Bk 34576 Pg 486), Covenants & Easements (Pg 477) and Restrictive Covenants (Pg 471) recorded at the Essex South Registry. Developer: DUC Residential LLC / Paul DiBiase; drafted by Brian McGrail.

t: Common land deeded to the HOA; First Amendment recorded
x: DUC Residential conveys Open Space Parcel C (5.04 ac, 100 Pond View) to the association for $1 (Bk 35266 Pg 472) and, the same day, records the First Amendment to the Trust (Bk 35266 Pg 467): mailbox and mailbox-post maintenance becomes a Trust purpose, with the City bearing no liability for plow/sanding damage. (The amendment surfaced in the 2026-07-17 registry sweep.)
Beverly Conservation Commission issues the WPA Form 8B with seven perpetual On-Going Conditions; recorded Bk 36443 Pg 213 (Dec 29, 2017).
The Appointment and Acceptance of Successor Trustees are executed, seating the first five-owner board for a two-year term (instruments recorded at the Registry in early 2018).
Paul DiBiase's resignation as developer-trustee and the successor-trustee appointments are recorded at the Essex South Registry — control of the association formally passes to the owners.
A trustee from #14 resigns from the board; the resignation instrument is recorded at the Registry on April 30, 2019.
A homeowner at #11 is appointed to the vacant trustee seat by per-household vote; the appointment instrument is recorded at the Registry.
A homeowner at #6 is appointed to a second board vacancy with more than 75% owner consent; the appointment instrument is recorded at the Registry in January 2020.
The #11 trustee's resignation is eRecorded at the Registry on October 15, 2019 — the same day as that home's sale.

t: Buffer-zone permitting done right — NOI → Order of Conditions
x: A homeowner planning a fenced terraced lawn in the buffer files a Notice of Intent (DEP #5-1341, prepared by Seekamp Environmental; ~600 sq ft of grading, the wetland ~30 ft below the yard). The Commission hears it and issues the Order of Conditions the same evening, 4-0 — and a complete Certificate of Compliance closes the file on an as-built in August 2022. The lane's model example of the buffer-zone process working.

t: After-the-fact filing regularizes completed patio work
x: Already-completed patio construction and landscaping at a home on the lane come to the Commission by an after-the-fact Request for Determination of Applicability (filed 11/19/2021). At a special meeting the Commission reviews the permeable construction and the 50-foot No-Build line and issues a Negative 3 Determination with conditions, 4-0 — retroactive approval is possible, but it runs through the same review.
A trustee from #16 resigns from the board; the resignation instrument is recorded at the Registry on November 19, 2021.

t: The fifth seat is filled — but not on the record
x: A successor trustee is appointed in 2022 to fill the seat left by the 2021 resignation, but no appointment instrument is recorded at the Registry. The last recorded appointment is from December 2019, so the recorded chain of board changes ends with the November 2021 resignation — the public record currently documents four of the five sitting trustees.

Beverly's assessed value of the 5-acre common parcel (100 Pond View Lane) drops from $75,600 to $0 beginning FY2023 and holds through FY2026 — the association's annual real-estate tax on the open space ends. The assessor database does not state the mechanism of the change.

t: Enforcement Order — unpermitted work on the common parcel
x: After the Conservation Agent identifies an unpermitted stone retaining wall on the intermittent stream bank and a patio in the buffer zone of the HOA's common parcel, the ConCom issues an Enforcement Order requiring an after-the-fact filing.

The ConCom resolves the common-parcel enforcement: the walls, patio, and knotweed management are permitted after the fact, with conditions — including no further alteration of areas under Commission jurisdiction on the parcel.

t: Nine-pine removal approved — Negative 3 with conditions
x: The association's Request for Determination of Applicability to remove nine dead pine trees on the common parcel (100 Pond View Lane) is heard and approved: a Negative 3 Determination of Applicability with conditions, on a 4-0 roll call. A trustee presents for the association; the Conservation Agent states he visited the site and believes the trees are dead. Conditions: nine replacement trees — all white pines, species to be finalized with Commission staff — photo documentation at the end of a two-year survival period, and all removal work from the paved surface of the cul-de-sac.
